newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sells 27 bln dong T-notes, rate 7.89 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sells 27 bln dong T-notes, rate 7.89 pct.

text.p: Vietnam sold 27 billion dong ($2.44 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes with an annual coupon of 7.89 percent to domestic institutions at an auction on Wednesday, the State Bank of Vietnam said in a statement.
At the last auction of government paper, on October 9, the central bank issued 70 billion dong worth of one-year notes at a rate of 7.90 percent.

The bank had originally said it would sell 70 billion dong of notes today. A state bank official said rate bids at the auction -- some of which were as high as nine percent -- were deemed too high, and so less stock was issued than originally planned.

Interest rates have fallen sharply this year, partly due to a dong surplus in the banking system but also because of a push by the government to bolster economic growth with easier monetary conditions.
At this year's first sale of Treasury stock, on March 1, the State Bank of Vietnam sold six-month bills at an annual rate of 15.00 percent.
One Treasury dealer at a foreign bank said it appeared that by cutting off bids at below the last sale's rate, the authorities appeared to be anxious not to signal an upturn in rates.
The issue date of the notes sold on Wednesday is October 25 and maturity will be on October 25, 1997.
The bank said allotments of stock, in dong, were as follows:
Nha Rong Joint-Stock Insurance Corp 12.0 billion
Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam 10.0 billion
National General Insurance Company of Vietnam 3.0 billion
